entries.159a5a5ce39d7ad9: The brands offered include Sukiya (beef bowls), Hama Sushi (conveyor-belt sushi), the take-out sushi brands centered on Europe and the Americas, namely “AFC (ZENSHI),” “SNOWFOX,” “YO!,” “Bento,” and “Sushi Circle,” Nakau (oyakodon and Kyoto-style udon), Zetteria (hamburgers), Coco's (family restaurants), and the supermarkets “Maruya” and “Joy Foods,” among others. Supporting this is what the securities report calls the “Mass Merchandising System (MMD),” a system that plans, designs and consistently controls the entire process from menu development to ingredient procurement, manufacturing and processing, logistics and sales. Its purpose is stated as “to provide safe and delicious food to people around the world at affordable prices.” Among these processes, food manufacturing and processing is handled by GFF Co., Ltd. (16 factories); ingredient procurement and sales by Zensho Shoji Co., Ltd.; logistics and nationwide delivery of ingredients by Global Fresh Supply Co., Ltd.; store equipment and maintenance by Techno Kensetsu Co., Ltd.; and procurement and sales of equipment and uniforms by Global Table Supply Co., Ltd. All of these are included in the reportable segment “Head Office & Support.” The group's total production value was ¥141,792 million (106.5% of the previous year), of which Head Office & Support accounted for ¥87,006 million.
entries.167f6a43246392b6: Zensho operates restaurants including Sukiya, Hama Sushi and Coco's through company-operated stores and franchises (FC), and handles everything from menu development to ingredient procurement, manufacturing and processing, logistics and sales, designing these processes within its own group. Its sources of revenue are three: serving food at restaurants, selling food products at supermarkets and other stores, and franchise joining fees and royalty income. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,264,053 million. Among its [[term:segment|reportable segments]], the one with the largest revenue from external customers was Global Hama Sushi, at ¥320,277 million, while the one with the largest operating profit was Global Takeout, which handles overseas take-out sushi, at ¥27,376 million.

entries.46761a63b31b8452: This business operates the beef bowl chain Sukiya directly in Japan, China, Southeast Asia and Central and South America. It serves a wide range of customers, including families and groups, with safe and tasty products at affordable prices, centered on its main beef bowl. It is operated by Sukiya Co., Ltd. and overseas subsidiaries such as Izumisei Catering (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., Taiwan Shanshang Co., Ltd., ZENSHO (THAILAND) CO., LTD. and ZENSHO DO BRASIL COMERCIO DE ALIMENTOS LTDA. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥314,454 million (up 6.3% year on year), and its share of group revenue was 24.9%. Operating profit was ¥9,317 million (down 62.0%). The number of stores at fiscal year-end was 2,650 (2,000 in Japan and 650 overseas), with 112 stores opened and 83 closed during the period. During this period, in addition to implementing beef bowl price cuts, it continued its health and safety measures following a foreign-matter contamination incident at some domestic stores at the end of the prior fiscal year, including strengthened cleaning and planned renovation of aging stores.

entries.4c34b832d31ac192: Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,264,053 million (up 11.2% from the previous year). According to the accounting policies in the securities report, there are three types of revenue. The first is serving food at restaurants; food is served based on customer orders, and revenue is recognized when the consideration is received. The second is sales of food products at supermarkets, sales of ingredients to FC members and others, and wholesale of processed foods; revenue is recognized when the goods are delivered. The third is FC franchise fees and royalty income; joining fees are recorded as advance receipts at contract signing and then recognized as revenue over a certain period, and royalties are measured based on the counterparty's sales, among other factors. The securities report does not show the amounts for these three types separately, so scale is viewed using revenue from external customers by reportable segment. The figures are as follows: Global Hama Sushi ¥320,277 million, Global Sukiya ¥314,454 million, Global Takeout ¥221,895 million, Restaurant ¥171,281 million, Global Fast Food ¥112,818 million, Retail ¥76,977 million, Other ¥35,638 million, and Head Office & Support ¥10,709 million. Head Office & Support's revenue from other segments within the group (intersegment internal revenue or transfers) was ¥481,411 million, larger than its revenue from external customers, and a note states that this internal revenue is based on prevailing market prices.

entries.4e44cddc1f0ba32e: This business operates sushi takeout stores and similar outlets, mainly in Europe and the United States, through directly operated stores and franchises (FC). The main brands are "AFC" and "ZENSHI" of Advanced Fresh Concepts Corp., "sushicircle" of Sushi Circle Gastronomie GmbH, and "SNOWFOX", "Bento", "Taiko", "YO!" and "SNOWFRUIT" of Wonderfield TopCo Limited. From the fiscal year ended March 2026, the overseas takeout sushi business, which had previously been included in "Global Fast Food", is separated and disclosed in this segment (the prior year's figures are also restated into the new segment). Sales to external customers were ¥221,895 million (up 5.7% year on year), and the share of group sales was 17.6%. Operating profit was ¥27,376 million (up 7.0%). The number of stores at the end of the period was 8,970 (including FC8,102 stores); 761 stores were opened and 1,306 stores were closed as store replacements based on profitability and location conditions.

entries.53b2545369346362: This business operates various kinds of fast food in Japan and overseas, including "Nakau" (oyakodon and Kyoto-style udon) and "Zetteria" (hamburgers). Sales to external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥112,818 million (up 8.3% year on year), and the share of group sales was 8.9%. Operating profit was ¥3,310 million (down 7.3%). entries.8647bdfb06f103d0: The securities report states: “The group consists of the company and 174 affiliated companies, for a total of 175, and conducts its food business management across a broad range.” The reportable [[term:segment|segments]] are seven: “Global Sukiya,” “Global Hama Sushi,” “Global Takeout,” “Global Fast Food,” “Restaurant,” “Retail,” and “Head Office & Support,” to which “Other” (manufacturing and wholesale, nursing care, livestock and marine products businesses, etc.), which is not included in the reportable segments, is added. From the fiscal year ended March 2026, the overseas take-out sushi business, previously included in “Global Fast Food,” is disclosed separately as “Global Takeout,” and the previous year's figures are also restated under this new classification. Although the name includes “Holdings,” the securities report's 【Status of Shareholdings】 section states that, based on the share of the company's total revenue accounted for by sales of ingredients and beverages to the group (wholesale business), the company recognizes wholesale business as its principal business.

entries.b92fab21f490af7e: For the fiscal year ended March 2026, operating profit was ¥81,440 million (up 8.4% from the previous year), ordinary profit was ¥78,257 million (up 8.9%), and profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥45,812 million (up 16.6%).
